_note: Industry definitions used in the trial. Text is a short paraphrase for the trial; production loads the official text from each source (US 311613 survey, research sources list). 'parents' is the crosswalk to CICTT parents agreed by SMEs (I-8).

definitions.source: ICAO Doc 9870, Manual on the Prevention of Runway Incursions
definitions.text: Any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for the landing and takeoff of aircraft.
Runway incursions are classified by cause as pilot deviations, operational incidents (controller actions) or vehicle and pedestrian deviations, and by severity from A to D.
A landing, attempted landing, line-up or takeoff on a surface other than the one assigned: a wrong runway, a taxiway, a closed runway or the wrong airport.

definitions.term: Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway
definitions.text: An aircraft, vehicle or person entering a runway or taxiway without authorization, or an aircraft using a taxiway or the wrong runway for landing or takeoff.
An aircraft leaves the runway surface during takeoff or landing, either by veering off the side or by overrunning the end.

definitions.source: ICAO Global Reporting Format (GRF) for runway surface conditions
definitions.text: A runway condition code from 6 (dry) down to 0 reports braking performance on wet or contaminated runways (water, slush, snow, ice), so crews can recompute landing distance.
An aircraft departs the runway surface during the takeoff or landing roll, including overruns after a long or fast landing.
A significant, unintended departure of the aircraft from controlled flight, such as a stall, spin or upset, often following a system malfunction or crew response to erroneous indications.
Erroneous or disagreeing airspeed indications, for example from pitot icing, ice crystals or a blocked pitot tube, which can lead to an upset if the crew follows the wrong indication.

definitions.source: ICAO Annex 10 – Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS)
definitions.text: An ACAS or TCAS indication to the flight crew recommending a vertical manoeuvre to increase separation from conflicting traffic.
An unauthorised vertical deviation of more than 300 feet from the cleared flight level or altitude, a common cause of loss of separation and TCAS resolution advisories.
Two aircraft in flight come into conflict or lose separation, including near midair collisions and TCAS events.
Turbulence in cloud-free air, often near jet streams or over mountains, with no visual cue and often not shown on weather radar.

definitions.source: FAA Advisory Circular 120-88A – Preventing Injuries Caused by Turbulence
definitions.text: Passengers and flight attendants are injured in turbulence mainly when standing or not wearing seat belts, and by unsecured carts and galley equipment.
A collision between an aircraft and a bird or other wildlife, including ingestion into an engine, reported with damage and phase of flight.
Engines must be shown to withstand the ingestion of birds of defined sizes; large or multiple bird ingestion can damage fan blades and cause surge, loss of thrust, shutdown or fire.

definitions.source: FAA holdover time guidelines (ground de-icing and anti-icing)
definitions.text: The estimated time a de-icing or anti-icing fluid protects aircraft surfaces from frost or ice; if it is exceeded before takeoff, the aircraft must be checked or de-iced again.

definitions.source: SKYbrary – Hard Landing and Tail Strike
definitions.text: A touchdown with a vertical load above limits, a bounced landing, or contact of the tail with the runway during takeoff rotation or landing flare.
